item: The lxml extraction is bracketed in RC2's native in-flight black box, inside the extraction lock
summary: extract_article wraps the locked extraction in native_call('lxml') (src/monitoring/native_inflight.py, a 128-byte memory-mapped counter file the next boot reads), directly inside _LXML_LOCK and around the whole _extract_locked call: the lock covers the parse, the walk and the release of the trees, and the faulting frame of the 2026-10-14 SIGABRT could be any of them. It sits after the live gauge's holding mark and before its released mark, on a return and on a raise, so those two stay the first statement of the hold and of its finally (the existing AST pin and a new ordering test). On a raise the bracket stays open while _release_frames frees the trees held by the traceback's frames (libxml2's free), so an abort there reads as lxml in flight; the first version closed it before that, found by the independent read. A worker waiting for the lock is not counted as in lxml, a raise leaves nothing in flight and still raises, an empty page never reaches the bracket. Counts only; the module never raises and never swallows the body's exception. Cost, measured alone (python -I, three runs, medians of 15 timed blocks of 20,000 calls): entering and leaving the bracket takes 3.38 to 3.53 microseconds against 0.34 to 0.36 for an empty context manager in the same loop, so about 3.0 to 3.2 microseconds per extraction, INSIDE the hold (two stores into the mapped file under the module's lock). Against the 4.3 to 4.8 ms of an 8 KB extraction and the 28 to 30 ms of a 64 KB one (micro_marks.py, on the gauge PR's head) that is about 0.07 and 0.01 percent; no pass-level run was made, the gauge's own A/B could not resolve a microsecond. Said plainly: this is the UNCONTENDED cost. The module's lock is shared with the socket guard's dns and connect brackets from every worker, so a hold that meets another thread inside it is longer and was not measured; and a store to the mapped page can fault into the filesystem after writeback, also not measured. The app opens the file at boot (session_hwm calls start()), so the first-call open does not fall inside a hold there. Proof: 8 tests (the slot counts one call in flight while the body runs and remembers the entry; a raising extraction leaves nothing in flight and the lock is given up; the bracket opens and closes with the lock held; the bracket sits between the gauge's holding and released marks on a return and on a raise; the trees of a returning and of a raising extraction are freed while the slot still counts the call; a worker waiting for the lock is not counted; an empty page never reaches the bracket); 7 mutants (bracket opened before holding, bracket not called, bracket outside the lock, bracket closed after released, the trees freed after the bracket closed, bracket left open on a raise, wrong slot), all killed. One independent Opus read: one should-fix (the trees-freed ordering above, folded), one test-hygiene fix (the waiting-worker test releases its thread in a finally, folded) and two notes on native_inflight.py itself (above, and a KeyboardInterrupt between the bump and the return of __enter__ would leave a count at 1 until restart, main thread only, reported to the module's owner).
